config.name: renderer-check
config.about: The known scenes and tolerances `renderer check` verifies stage 1 of the training renderer with: the rounded rectangle with fill and opacity. A scene marked on_kinks has edges on pixel boundaries or a value on one of its bounds, where a gradient is one-sided, so finite differences are not taken there. Every other scene's numbers are chosen so that, at each scale, no edge and no centre of a corner's circle falls on a pixel's boundary or centre: a central difference taken exactly where the cover changes from one formula to the next is wrong in proportion to its step, whatever the gradient. A scene marked leaves_viewport is not a valid scene and is never drawn by the runtime renderer.

scenes.name: overlaps
scenes.about: Translucent and opaque elements over one another, in drawing order.

scenes.name: radii
scenes.about: Corner radii from under a pixel to nearly a circle.

scenes.name: thin
scenes.about: Dividers thinner than a pixel, and one a pixel thick.

scenes.name: square-corners
scenes.about: No corner radius anywhere: translucent boxes over one another and dividers thinner than a pixel, off the pixel grid. A radius of zero is on its bound.

scenes.name: past-the-viewport
scenes.about: Elements that cross each edge of the viewport and one corner, as a prediction may. Not a valid scene.

scenes.name: whole-numbers
scenes.about: As a true scene is written: a surface that fills the viewport, boxes on whole numbers that meet edge to edge and touch the viewport's edges, square corners, a pill, an element of no opacity.

moves.name: across
moves.about: An element that overlaps its target moves onto it.

moves.name: diagonal
moves.about: It moves on both axes at once.

moves.name: size
moves.about: It grows to its target's size.

moves.name: corner-radius
moves.about: Its corners round to its target's.

moves.name: fill
moves.about: Its colour and alpha change to its target's.

moves.name: opacity
moves.about: It fades in to its target's opacity.

moves.name: everything
moves.about: Every value moves at once, over a backdrop that does not. The element starts inside its target, in a colour nearer the target's than the backdrop's.

zero_gradients.name: no-overlap-with-the-target
zero_gradients.about: A square-cornered element and its target do not touch. Moving it changes which pixels differ and not how much, so position has no gradient. Neither has a corner radius of zero: rounding a square corner a little takes away an area that grows as the radius squared. Size, fill and opacity have one.

zero_gradients.name: rounded-without-overlap
zero_gradients.about: The same with rounded corners. An arc is drawn as its tangent, so the element's whole cover changes a little with where its corners fall among the pixels, and position has a small gradient that the shape itself does not: a limit of this renderer, measured here.

zero_gradients.name: under-an-opaque-element
zero_gradients.about: The element lies wholly under a later opaque one, so nothing about it reaches a pixel.

zero_gradients.name: no-opacity
zero_gradients.about: The element has no opacity, so nothing about its shape or colour reaches a pixel; its opacity does.

definitions.finite_difference: (f(v + step) - f(v - step)) / (2 step), one number at a time, on the CPU in 64-bit floats
definitions.passes: |autograd - other| <= absolute_tolerance + relative_tolerance * |other|, for every number of the attribute
definitions.render_loss: the mean of |image - target image| over every channel of every pixel, both drawn by the training renderer
definitions.gradient_state: disconnected: the number is not part of the computation. zero: it is, and every part of its gradient is within zero_tolerance of zero. non-zero: otherwise.
definitions.levels: differences between images are in levels of 255 over RGBA with colour premultiplied by alpha
definitions.mean_absolute_difference: mean of |a - b| over every channel of every pixel
definitions.share_of_pixels_over_16: share of pixels in which some channel differs by more than 16 levels
definitions.largest_difference: largest |a - b| of any channel of any pixel
definitions.exact_cover: each pixel's cover by each element counted from exact_cover_samples sample points, no two in one column or row of the pixel, then composited as both renderers composite; computed here with numpy
definitions.verified: drawn is verified when the Apple GPU path's image agrees with the CPU's and agreement with the runtime renderer was measured; an attribute is verified when its finite differences pass on the CPU and its gradient on the Apple GPU path agrees with the CPU's

scalars.squared_difference_from_target: the sum of (image - target image) squared over every channel of every pixel
scalars.weighted_sum: the sum of the image times fixed pseudo-random weights in -1 to 1

support_matrix.primitive: rounded rectangle with fill and opacity

limits: An arc is drawn as its tangent, which never covers less than the arc: a corner of radius under about two pixels is drawn too full on its own few pixels, and a rounded element's whole cover changes a little with where its corners fall among the pixels.
Position, size and corner radius receive a gradient only from the pixels the outline crosses. An element that shares no differing pixel with its target has no gradient in position.
A corner radius past half the box's shorter side is drawn as that half and receives no gradient; a prediction is kept inside the bound to be learned.
A box with a width or height at or below zero draws nothing and receives no gradient.
Colour channels and opacity are used as given, in or out of 0 to 1.
Drawing order is the order the elements are given in and receives no gradient.

apple_gpu_path.statement: Forward and backward ran on the Apple GPU path with no unsupported operation and no CPU fallback.
